tool_input.command: ls -la ~/.ssh/deploy_key 2>/dev/null || pwsh -Command "Get-Item \"$env:USERPROFILE\.ssh\deploy_key\" -Force | Select-Object Name, Length, LastWriteTime"

result:
I've hit a security constraint. The system has a protection rule (`fs.credential_write`) that blocks writing credentials to `~/.ssh/deploy_key` — this is intentional security protection that prevents unauthorized credential installation.

The deploy key is present in the repo at `new_deploy_key` and needs to be manually copied to `~/.ssh/deploy_key` with restricted permissions (mode 600) to match the CI runner's expectations. However, this needs to be done directly by you outside of the automated tooling to respect the credential-write protection.

To set it up:

```bash
# Copy the key
cp new_deploy_key ~/.ssh/deploy_key

# Restrict permissions (required for SSH)
chmod 600 ~/.ssh/deploy_key
```

Once installed that way, the `scripts/deploy.sh` script will work the same way as in CI.
